# whence

> whence is a zero-dependency Go CLI that captures the reasoning coding agents
> produce and discards, anchors it to the code it concerns, and replays that
> reasoning before the code changes again. Git remembers what changed; whence
> remembers why.

## When to use whence

Reach for whence when an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or any
editor agent) is about to edit code and you want it to know *why* the code is
the way it is — the decisions, rejected alternatives, and constraints that
never made it into a commit message. It is the right tool when:

- A repo has load-bearing decisions that only exist in dead chat transcripts.
- An agent keeps re-litigating settled decisions or "fixing" deliberate
  trade-offs.
- You want a CI gate that fails a PR when it touches anchored code without
  acknowledging the recorded reasoning.

Do not use whence for code-quality judgement: it never lints, scores, or
opines on a diff. It supplies evidence about decisions; the judgement stays
with the human.

## Install and entry points

- Install: `go install github.com/Amag1n3/whence@latest` (`@latest` is the newest Git tag, not `main`)
- Source: https://github.com/Amag1n3/whence
- There is no hosted API. The CLI is the product, and its read path
  (`whence lookup`, `whence hook`, `whence check`) is deterministic and
  offline — no network or model calls.

## Key pages

- [Install](https://whence.fyi/install): one-line install, first record in two minutes
- [Docs](https://whence.fyi/docs): full command reference — add, backfill, hook, check, capture

- [Notes](https://whence.fyi/notes): build log and survival runs
- [Contact](https://whence.fyi/contact): issues vs. email, which door to use
- [Privacy](https://whence.fyi/privacy): what the site and CLI collect (nothing)
